text: Employee compensation / GOS / net-tax shares in 2024 are 33.6 / 63.6 / 2.8 and in 2025 are 33.9 / 62.0 / 4.1 percent of nominal GDP.
limitations: National income shares, not household incomes or AI effects.

text: The employee-compensation share increased by 0.3 percentage point.
limitations: 33.9 minus 33.6, using rounded published shares; not 0.3 percent growth.

text: Compensation includes pay, benefits in kind and employer contributions; GOS includes mixed income and depreciation.
locator: Section 3, PDF p. 2; statistical discrepancy discussion p. 3
limitations: GOS is not simply corporate profit; mixed income contains owner/household labor.

text: The IMF reports 27% high-exposure low-complementarity and 20% high-exposure high-complementarity among all employed.
limitations: Historical employment estimates extrapolated to 2018; not realized displacement or wage gains.

text: The IMF reports the high-exposure low-complementarity category for about 40% of employed women and 20% of employed men.
limitations: Denominators are employed people within each sex; not individual job-loss probabilities.

text: The IMF extrapolates fixed detailed 2000 occupational shares to broad 2018 employment totals.
limitations: Fixed within-category shares were not independently validated here; not 2026 workforce measurement.

text: Rosli argues that exposure cannot attribute job losses to AI without adoption-linked outcome data.
limitations: Attributed methodological commentary; not independent causal evidence and not proof of no harm.
